subject.title: Feature request: Auto-send intent/acknowledgment text message before agent processing

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a broad `messages.ackText` config, as a non-terminal plugin/channel hook, or only through channel-specific placeholder features?
rationale: The requested behavior adds new visible chat behavior and a config or plugin API contract across multiple channel owners, which automation should not choose without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Design Broad Ack Text Contract
options.body: Add a default-off cross-channel acknowledgement text contract with clear scope semantics and channel capability fallbacks.

options.title: Expose A Non-Terminal Hook
options.body: Add a plugin/channel hook that can send an interim message and continue normal dispatch without making global text config the first API.

options.title: Use Channel-Specific Placeholders
options.body: Keep this issue as product context while Slack, Discord, Telegram, and other channels decide their own placeholder lifecycles separately.

recommendation.title: Design Broad Ack Text Contract
recommendation.body: Add a default-off cross-channel acknowledgement text contract with clear scope semantics and channel capability fallbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing evidence is recent work on reply lifecycle, source delivery, Slack dispatch, and the previous review of this exact cross-channel gap.
